# A test build on fyne queues what an answer posts back to the drawing
# thread, and a test's wait runs it. What the last test's Model posted and the
# last test never waited for is dropped as the next test starts, since that
# test starts from a fresh Model: run, it drew the last Model's widgets inside
# the next test's waits, and a wait ran out.
#
# The first test asks twenty questions, each answer's handler slow, and waits
# for the first answer alone; the rest have arrived while that handler ran.
# The second, run next on the same component and so in the same program,
# waits a second for the one answer it asks for, which the twenty would have
# queued behind.
#
# fyne alone: every other target's test driver draws an answer in well under
# the time this one takes, and so none of them waits behind the last test.

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +2 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import async "sngl:async"
import http "sngl:http"
import seq "sngl:seq"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func lookup(k string) async.Result[string] {
    match var r = http.get(url="http://127.0.0.1:47819/status/200") {
        failed { return {failed=r} }
        ok { return {ok=k} }
    }
}

// Work that takes a while, and returns something so it is not left out.
func spin(n int) int {
    var total = 0
    for var i = seq.count(n) {
        total = (total + i) % 7919
    }
    return total
}

// A page asking one question as it opens, and twenty more, each answer's
// handler slow, once `ask` is clicked.
component page ui.node {
    var answer option[string] = null
    var asking = false
    var answered = 0
    var spun = 0

    async.query(on="one", fetch=lookup, :value=answer)
    if asking {
        for var i = seq.count(20) {
            async.query(on="{i}", fetch=lookup, @load(got) {
                spun += spin(60000000 + got.length())
                answered += 1
            })
        }
    }
    ui.text(value=answer != null ? answer : "-")
    ui.button #ask(text="Ask", @click { asking = true })
}

func testAFirstAnswer(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.ask.click()
    t.wait(func() => c.answered > 0, 20000)
    t.assert(c.answered > 0 && c.answered < 20)
}

func testBTheNextTestWaitsForItsOwnAnswerAlone(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.wait(func() => c.answer != null, 1000)
    t.assert(c.answer != null && c.answer == "one")
}

ui.window {
    page()
}
